description: Scaffold the laya-browser-mcp TypeScript/Node 22 project AND design the core data shapes first (Foundational Thinking: scaffold before feature, types before logic). Establish the toolchain (pnpm, tsc ESM, vitest), install verified dependencies, get a green baseline (typecheck + build + one trivial passing test), and land the pure core type module that every later phase depends on. Also run the time-boxed web-agent ONNX-export spike and record its result. Independent of other features (they build on it).
steps: Initialize package.json at repo root: name 'laya-browser-mcp', type 'module', engines.node '>=20', bin { 'laya-browser-mcp': 'dist/index.js' }, scripts: build='tsc -p tsconfig.json', typecheck='tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit', test='vitest run', 'test:watch'='vitest', start='node dist/index.js'.

Add dependencies (verified available on npm): runtime deps @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (^1.30), playwright (^1.63), @receptron/laya (^0.1.2), zod (for tool input schemas). devDeps: typescript (^5), vitest (^3 or latest), @types/node. Use pnpm. Run 'pnpm install' then 'pnpm exec playwright install chromium'.
Create tsconfig.json: target ES2022, module NodeNext, moduleResolution NodeNext, strict true, outDir dist, rootDir src, declaration true, esModuleInterop true, skipLibCheck true.
Create vitest.config.ts (test dir 'test', globals true, environment node, test timeout generous e.g. 30000 for browser tests).

DESIGN CORE TYPES in src/types.ts (the data shape handed to Laya + decision results). Define: (a) Ref = branded string like `e5`; (b) Control = { ref: Ref, index: number, role: string, name: string, tag: string, type?: string, value?: string, options?: string[], editable: boolean, checked?: boolean, disabled?: boolean }; (c) PageState = { goal: string, url: string, title: string, visibleText: string, controls: Control[], recentActions: string[] }; (d) Operation = 'CLICK'|'TYPE_TEXT'|'SELECT'|'SCROLL_DOWN'|'WAIT'|'DONE'|'BLOCKED' (mirror abedinia/laya-web-agent exactly); (e) Decision = { operation: Operation, operationConfidence: number, target?: Ref, targetConfidence: number, value?: string, source: 'laya'|'rule'|'llm'|'stub' } — make illegal states hard: a CLICK/TYPE_TEXT/SELECT decision should carry a target; DONE/BLOCKED/SCROLL_DOWN/WAIT need not. (f) LayaDecisionEngine interface: { decide(state: PageState): Promise<Decision>; readonly available: boolean; close(): Promise<void> } so the real engine and the stub are interchangeable (Type System Discipline / Boundary Discipline). Keep this module PURE (no playwright/onnx imports).
Add a trivial vitest test test/types.test.ts that constructs a PageState and asserts literal values, so the baseline test command is green and meaningful.

SPIKE (time-box ~15-20 min, do NOT let it block delivery): attempt to export abedinia/laya-web-agent (mmBERT-base) to an ONNX bundle usable by @receptron/laya's modelDir option. The @receptron/laya export script (export/export_onnx.py) is written for the ModernBERT checkpoint convaiinnovations/laya; the web-agent is mmBERT-base with max_len 2048/head_max_len 512. Try: create a python venv (uv or pyenv), pip install torch transformers safetensors onnx onnxscript onnxruntime huggingface_hub, snapshot_download('abedinia/laya-web-agent'), and run the receptron export_onnx.py against it. Record in docs/PLAN.md whether it (i) exported and loaded via Laya.load({modelDir}) [VERIFIED], (ii) partially worked, or (iii) failed — and if it failed, note the documented fallback (thin local Python sidecar using the `laya` pip package, which loses the no-Python-at-runtime property). If the download/compute is too heavy or fails in the environment, mark the spike INCONCLUSIVE with the exact error and proceed; the product must still work with a stub and with the reference receptron checkpoint via modelDir.

Create docs/PLAN.md capturing: the phased plan (phases 0-5), the core data shapes (PageState/Control/Decision/LayaDecisionEngine) with a short rationale, the spike result labeled VERIFIED/INFERRED/GUESSED/INCONCLUSIVE, and known risks (web-agent real-site reliability ~1/5 steps; ONNX export uncertainty; weights size).
acceptance_criteria: pnpm run typecheck passes with zero errors.
pnpm run build produces dist/ with compiled JS and .d.ts.
pnpm run test runs vitest and test/types.test.ts passes.
src/types.ts exports PageState, Control, Decision, Operation, and the LayaDecisionEngine interface, and imports neither playwright nor onnx.
docs/PLAN.md exists and records the spike outcome with an explicit VERIFIED/INFERRED/GUESSED/INCONCLUSIVE label and the fallback if applicable.
.gitignore excludes node_modules, dist, and the large ONNX weight files.
verification: Run 'pnpm run typecheck' and confirm zero errors.
Run 'pnpm run build' and confirm dist/index files are emitted (or at least the compiled type module for this phase).
Run 'pnpm run test' and confirm the baseline test passes.
findings:
Scaffold complete and all acceptance criteria met. Created package.json (name laya-browser-mcp, type module, engines.node >=20, bin laya-browser-mcp -> dist/index.js, scripts build/typecheck/test/test:watch/start), tsconfig.json (ES2022, NodeNext, strict, declaration, outDir dist/rootDir src), vitest.config.ts (dir test, globals, node env, 30000ms timeout), .gitignore (node_modules, dist, coverage, *.onnx, *.onnx.data, model/, .venv), README.md, docs/PLAN.md, src/types.ts, test/types.test.ts. Installed verified deps via pnpm: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.1, @receptron/laya 0.1.2, playwright 1.63.0, zod 3.25.76; dev typescript 5.9.3, vitest 3.2.7, @types/node 22.20.4. Ran pnpm exec playwright install chromium (OK). VERIFICATION: pnpm run typecheck = zero errors; pnpm run build emits dist/types.{js,d.ts,*.map}; pnpm run test = 3/3 pass. Note: dist/index.js does not exist yet (src/index.ts is a later phase) — bin target will resolve once server phase lands; acceptance criterion allows 'or at least the compiled type module for this phase'.

TYPES DESIGN: src/types.ts is PURE (no playwright/onnx imports; grep-confirmed). Ref is a branded string with asRef() helper. Control has ref/index(1-based)/role/name/tag/type?/value?/options?/editable/checked?/disabled?. PageState = goal/url/title/visibleText/controls/recentActions. Operation is the exact 7-member web-agent set. Decision is a DISCRIMINATED UNION making illegal states unrepresentable: CLICK/TYPE_TEXT/SELECT require target:Ref (+ optional value); DONE/BLOCKED/SCROLL_DOWN/WAIT forbid target/value. LayaDecisionEngine = { decide(state):Promise<Decision>; readonly available:boolean; close():Promise<void> } so real engine and stub are interchangeable.

SPIKE RESULT = VERIFIED (end-to-end, with one small documented tokenizer fix). Using Python 3.12 (uv venv) + torch 2.14/transformers 5.17/onnx/onnxscript/onnxruntime/safetensors/huggingface_hub: (1) snapshot_download('abedinia/laya-web-agent') — its encoder/config.json is model_type modernbert / ModernBertForMaskedLM (trained from mmBERT-base per rl_agent_config.json but shipped ModernBERT-shaped; hidden 768, 22 layers, vocab 256000, max_len 2048/head_max_len 512), file layout matches convaiinnovations/laya. The web-agent repo does NOT ship rl_common.py/rl_agent_api.py/email_utils.py so I pulled them from convaiinnovations/laya. (2) Ran receptron export/export_onnx.py UNMODIFIED against the web-agent files -> EXPORTED successfully, PyTorch parity max|dlogits|=2.48e-05, max|dact|=0.0; bundle = laya.onnx 1291MB (inline weights, external_data=False so no separate laya.onnx.data needed for modelDir path) + laya_config.json + tokenizer/. (3) Rebuilt onnxruntime-node native binding (pnpm rebuild) and tried Laya.load({modelDir}) in Node -> FAILED 'special token [CLS] missing from tokenizer' because @receptron/laya@0.1.2 hardcodes ModernBERT special-token names [CLS]/[SEP]/[MASK]/[PAD] but the web-agent tokenizer names them <bos>(2)/<eos>(1)/<mask>(4)/<pad>(0). (4) Renamed those 4 special-token contents in tokenizer/tokenizer.json to [CLS]/[SEP]/[MASK]/[PAD] (SAME token IDs) -> Laya.load({modelDir}) then LOADED and RAN: a narrow choice question over the exact web-agent operation set returned a calibrated distribution (CLICK 0.53, SELECT 0.33, DONE 0.07, ...), input_tokens 105, close() clean. CONCLUSION: web-agent runs on-device via @receptron/laya with NO Python at runtime, provided the export/prepare step also remaps tokenizer special-token names (IDs unchanged) — a one-line rename, no @receptron/laya code change, ONNX graph untouched. Fallback (not needed): thin local Python sidecar using the laya pip package (loses no-Python-at-runtime). Product works regardless via stub engine (tests) and the reference receptron checkpoint via modelDir. All ~1.3-1.7GB spike artifacts and the 5.5GB .venv were deleted after the spike; also cleaned stray checkpoint files that an early botched heredoc had dumped into the repo root. ENV NOTE for later features: /tmp is NOT persistent across separate execute_bash calls in this sandbox — do heavy download+use in a single call or work under the repo dir; and onnxruntime-node build script is ignored by pnpm on install (run 'pnpm rebuild onnxruntime-node' before using the real engine).
